surface_mechanism_description: The self-limiting reaction between source materials and the GaAs surface, where TEG and arsine can be used to realize the ALE of GaAs under proper growth conditions. The dissociative adsorption of TEG (or its radical) occurs only on the As-terminated sites, preventing further adsorption of MOs and their radicals.
evidence: The self-limiting reaction which leads to ALE is built-in in the way TEG reacts with GaAs surfaces at low temperatures. Presently there are two models for ALE growth of GaAs using metalorganic compounds (MOs). One is based on the adsorption of radicals of MOS. Here partially cracked radicals (for example, monomethylgallium for example in the case of TMG) are adsorbed at the surface sites forming a radical terminated surface which prevents further adsorption of MOs and their radicals. The other model is based on the 'site selective decomposition' of MOs or their radicals. Here MOs and their radicals are decomposed to metal (for example, Ga) only when they land on As atoms. In an effort to unveil the mechanism of ALE, a clean arsenic-stabilized GaAs surface grown by MBE was exposed to TEG gas and subsequent change was analyzed by in situ x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS).
